label: r2c2
name: global trunk + per-layer head
hypothesis: Feeds the r1c2 trunk (dilated residual convolution plus a broadcast global vector, so every cell sees the whole grid) into the r1c3 per-layer footprint head. Each layer's score can then depend on global build progress and on what is still missing elsewhere, which matters for build order. The per-layer head keeps landing-layer reasoning explicit. Compute is about 1.4x. Refuted if it scores at or below both r1c2 and r1c3.
last_analysis: Scores are hidden, so the only evidence is that every trial trained without errors. No result has been refuted. Two ideas in the plan are layer-relative: scoring placements separately for each layer and taking a logsumexp over layers, and using relative-height inputs. Both fit the task, because whether a brick is correct depends on its landing layer, the cells below it that it would seal, and the cells above it that it would block. Using 2 PPO epochs gives nearly twice the fresh designs at about the same number of gradient steps. With only 3 trials left, I keep the r2c3 design (layer-mixing, 2 epochs) as the anchor and make one change in each candidate: (a) a lower entropy bonus, since evaluation is greedy and the action space is large; (b) the relative z-window input from r3c3 combined with layer-mixing; (c) per-layer features fed into the DONE and value heads, so stopping can depend on whether a good placement remains. With 2 seeds and possible seed-luck failures, small differences will be hard to separate.
